- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates drop; adjust downward by 2–5% of recent range.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 1–3% from forecast for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa), model lags by 1–3 days; align forecast with sentiment change by 1–2 days ahead or delay by 1–2 days.
- If model shows steady upward trend but true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline), reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model often fails to capture volatility; add ±1–2% buffer to forecast for uncertainty.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from model, check sentiment history for recent divergence; if sentiment is weak, reduce forecast by 5–10% to align with mean reversion bias.
